technical_facts: The product was renamed to 'Quake Arena'
The game will focus exclusively on deathmatch style gaming, including CTF
Single player mode will consist of aranking ranking ladder against bot AIs
Client-server communications channel limitations historically discouraged massive quantities of moving entities in single player
The graphics engine will be OpenGL only
The graphics engine will include fallback modes to render at Quake-2 quality and speed
personality_patterns: Prioritizes purity of focus over feature bloat
Willing to gamble on a design shift to achieve higher quality
Pragmatic approach to graphics technology, prioritizing framerate over visual richness for multiplayer
Iterative mindset regarding product vision (changing minds based on on new goals)

gnosis_principles.description: Concentrating on a specific core experience (multiplayer) to achieve significant advances rather than splitting resources across conflicting goals (single-player vs multiplayer).
In multiplayer gaming, once the initial visual impression is made, the speed of the game (framerate) is more important than rich visual scenes that compromise performance.

heritage_patterns: Separation of game rules from unit goals
Use of OpenGL as a primary graphics API
Developing fallback modes for hardware compatibility
Prioritizing network synchronization over entity density

dpo_pairs.prompt: Why did Carmack decide to move away from single-player FPS elements in Quake Arena?
dpo_pairs.chosen: To achieve a purity of focus that allows for significant advances in the multiplayer experience and to resolve conflicts between single-player and multiplayer design goals, such as communication channel limits and development time allocation.
dpo_pairs.rejected: Because he didn't like single-player games anymore.
